name: UXLoom

hlido_opinion.headline: A design-time critic for AI-generated UI that checks state coverage deterministically — unusually honest about being a linter, not a generator.
hlido_opinion.body: UXLoom occupies a genuinely under-served slot: everyone is shipping UI generators, almost nobody is shipping the thing that audits their output. It takes a journey definition (an open format the project calls JourneyGraph) plus the screens a generator produced, models the flow as a state machine, and reports what is missing — unreachable screens, dead-end transitions, absent loading/empty/error/offline states, WCAG contrast failures, sub-44px touch targets, and label overflow under localization growth. The public surface is precise about what that means: five named checks, a worked coverage matrix showing 21/30 required states on a sample checkout flow, and an explicit framing of the findings as deterministic — same input, same report, diffable in CI. That framing is the strongest signal here. A tool that says 'zero opinions, all evidence' and then shows you the matrix is making a claim you can falsify, which is rarer in this category than it should be. The distribution posture is equally clean for agent use: MIT, on npm, listed in the official MCP registry, no sign-up and no mailing list gate on the docs. What we cannot assess from the public surface is the part that decides whether it works — how well the journey definition survives contact with a real generator's output, and whether the required-state model is right for flows more complex than checkout. The site shows the sample, not the corpus. At v0.14 the honest read is a well-specified early tool with a real thesis, not a proven one.

tier_rationale: STEADY (71) because the value proposition is specific and independently checkable, the checks described are deterministic rather than model-judgement, and the access path is completely open — MIT, npm, MCP registry, docs with no login. It is not VITAL because the evidence on the public surface is a single illustrative flow rather than results across real projects, the version (v0.14) is pre-1.0 with the API surface still moving, and nothing public establishes how the journey definition holds up on flows the authors did not design the example around.
what_it_does_well: Names a real, specific gap — generators emit the happy path, nothing audits the missing states
Checks are deterministic and diffable, so findings are reviewable in CI rather than advisory
Publishes a worked coverage matrix (21/30 states) instead of only asserting the capability
Fully open access path: MIT, npm, official MCP registry, docs without sign-up
Explicitly positions as a critic layer over any generator rather than replacing one
what_it_fails_at: Evidence is one illustrative checkout flow — no results across real or third-party projects
v0.14 pre-1.0: the JourneyGraph format and CLI surface are not stability-committed
Requires the user to author a journey definition; the cost of that step is not shown
No pricing or commercial-support story published (fine for OSS, unclear for adoption)
The required-state model is asserted, not justified — why these states, for which flows, is undocumented on the surface
best_for: Teams shipping UI from v0, Lovable, Figma Make or Claude who need a gate before implementation
Design-system owners wanting state coverage enforced mechanically rather than by review
CI pipelines that can consume a deterministic report and fail a build on it
Agent workflows that generate UI and need a machine-checkable critic in the loop
not_recommended_for: Teams wanting UI generated rather than audited — this deliberately does not generate
Projects with no journey definition and no appetite to author one
Anyone needing production-stability guarantees today (pre-1.0, v0.14)
Accessibility programmes needing full WCAG audit coverage — this checks contrast and target size, not the standard

evidence_urls.claim: Checks journey completeness, state coverage, WCAG contrast, touch targets and text expansion
Published on npm and the official MCP registry
MIT licensed, no sign-up and no mailing list required
Sample coverage matrix reports 21/30 required states (70%)

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: CLI (npx uxloom check ./design) plus an MCP server listed in the official registry, so an agent can run the check and consume a structured report directly. The deterministic output is the property that makes it usable in an agent loop — a generating agent can call it, read the missing-state list, and iterate without a human arbitrating.

checklist.evidence: 'Your generator gave you 6 screens. UXLoom proves you're missing 9 states.'
Worked coverage matrix + sample CLI output on homepage
Docs linked in top nav, no login

marking_signal.note: No statement about marking or provenance of AI-generated output; the product audits UI rather than generating content.

pricing_facts.basis: Derived from Hlido-held evidence only (engine checklist + editorial text); quotes are verbatim from the scorecard; not vendor-supplied; re-derived daily. Verify current prices on the vendor's pricing page.
